metas.name: Açai Palm (Belém Palm)
metas.note: The species is native to eastern Amazonia, especially in Brazil, mainly in swamps and floodplains.
metas.footer: Click -> Euterpe Oleracea for more information!

metas.name: Acrocomia Totai (Paraguay Palm)
metas.note: Found in eastern Bolivia, Paraguay, northern Argentina and southern Brazil (Matto Grosso do Sul). It is commonly mistaken to be a Macaw Palm (Acrocomia Aculeata). The key difference is that the trunk of the "Paraguay Palm" is often smoother and less irregular. The crown can also give some hints although it's difficult to catch the differences - Macaw Palm: More open and irregular, with leaves spreading in different directions. - "Paraguay Palm": Denser and more compact, sometimes looking neater and rounder.
metas.footer: Click -> Acrocomia Totai for more information!

metas.name: African Oil Palm
metas.note: Elaeis Guineensis is an oil palm native to west and southwest Africa, specifically the area between Angola and The Gambia. The species is also now naturalised in many places, the most useful for Geoguessr are: Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, Cambodia, Sri Lanka and Central America.
metas.footer: Click -> Elaeis Guineensis for more information!

metas.name: African Palmyra Palm
metas.note: It is widespread across much of tropical Africa from Senegal to Uganda and south to northern South Africa.
metas.footer: Click -> Borassus Aethiopum for more information!

metas.name: Alexandra Palm
metas.note: The native range of this species is north-east and central-east Queensland, from the Melville Range in Cape York Peninsula to south of Gladstone.
metas.footer: Click -> Archontophoenix Alexandrae for more information!

metas.name: Areca Palm
metas.note: Areca catechu is a species of palm native to the Philippines cultivated for areca nuts. It is widespread in cultivation and is considered naturalized in Malaysia, Indonesia, Taiwan, Cambodia, Laos, Thailand, India (Assam and Kerala mostly), Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, and more regions that are not in Geoguessr.
metas.footer: Click -> Areca Catechu for more information!

metas.name: Asian Palmyra Palm (Cambodia Palm)
metas.note: Borassus Flabellifer is a fan palm native to South Asia especially Cambodia, Thailand, Bangladesh, India, Sri lanka, Indonesia (lesser nusa islands)
metas.footer: Click -> Borassus Flabellifer for more information!

metas.name: Babassu
metas.note: The Babassu is a palm native to the Amazon Rainforest region in South America. It is the predominant species in the Maranhão Babaçu forests of Brazil. It is also seen in amazonian states and rarely in Piauí and Tocantins. Not to be confused with other Attalea species like A. Phalerata and A.
metas.footer: Click -> Attalea Speciosa for more information!

metas.name: Cabbage Palmetto
metas.note: Sabal palmetto is native to the subtropical coastal regions of the American states of Florida, Georgia, South Carolina, southeastern North Carolina, and extreme southern Texas. It is very similar to its relatives S. Yapa, S. Mexicana, S. Rosei
metas.footer: Click -> Sabal Palmetto for more information!

metas.name: California Fan Palm
metas.note: Washingtonia filifera is the only palm native to the Western United States and one of the country's largest native palms.
metas.footer: Click -> Washingtonia Filifera for more information!

metas.name: Canary Island Palm
metas.note: Phoenix Canariensis is native to the Canary Islands but is typically cultivated in wet-winter or Mediterranean climates and also in wet-summer or humid subtropical climates. It appears in many notable examples of landscaping, particularly in the American state of California.
metas.footer: Click -> Phoenix Canariensis for more information!

metas.name: Caranday Palm
metas.note: Copernicia Alba is found in the Humid Chaco ecoregion in Bolivia, Paraguay, southern Brazil and northern Argentina. It can be hard to differenciate between C. Prunifera and C. Alba, one clue is that the C. Prunifera very often has visible gaps between the leaves, while the C. Alba has thicker, more densely packed leaves. The best way to identify them though is trying to tell by the landscape - if you're in northern Brazil or not.
metas.footer: Click -> Copernicia Alba for more information!

metas.name: Carnauba Palm (Ceará Palm)
metas.note: Copernicia Prunifera is a species of palm tree native to northeastern Brazil (mainly the states of Ceará, Piauí, Maranhão, Rio Grande do Norte and Bahia). It can be hard to differenciate between C. Prunifera and C. Alba, one clue is that the C. Prunifera very often has visible gaps between the leaves, while the C. Alba has thicker, more densely packed leaves. The best way to identify them though is trying to tell by the landscape - if you're in northern Brazil or not.
metas.footer: Click -> Copernicia Prunifera for more information!

metas.name: Chilean Wine Palm
metas.note: It is endemic to a small area of central Chile between southern Coquimbo, Valparaíso, Santiago, O'Higgins, and northern Maule regions. They are highly concentrated around Viña del Mar.
metas.footer: Click -> Jubaea Chilensis for more information!

metas.name: Chinese Fan Palm
metas.note: It is native to southern Japan, Taiwan, the Ryukyu Islands, and other regions that are not in Geoguessr.
metas.footer: Click -> Livistona Chinensis for more information!

metas.name: Doum Palm
metas.note: It is a native to the Arabian Peninsula and also to the northern half and western part of Africa. If you see this palm in India, you will most likely be in the union territory of Daman and Diu (or close to it, in coastal Gujarat).
metas.footer: Click -> Hyphaene Thebaica for more information!

metas.name: East African Doum Palm
metas.note: This is a palm known for its unique branching, unlike most palms which are not branched. It is very abundant in Kenya, and also found in other countries not featured in Geoguessr.
metas.footer: Click -> Hyphaene Compressa for more information!

metas.name: Florida Thatch Palm
metas.note: In the wild, this species almost always grows close to coastal areas. It is mostly found in southern Florida, Caribbean islands, and the eastern coast of the Yucatán peninsula in México. The key element to identify this palm between others found in similar areas, is the circular, fan shaped leaves.
metas.footer: Click -> Thrinax Radiata for more information!

metas.name: Ilala Palm
metas.note: The ilala palm is a species of palm tree native to the eastern Afrotropics. It occurs in Kwazulu-Natal (South Africa), the coastal flats of Madagascar and other countries that are not in Geoguessr.
metas.footer: Click -> Hyphaene Coriacea for more information!

metas.name: Juçara Palm
metas.note: Closely related to the Açaí palm, they are really hard to distinguish apart from each other. However, the Açaí palm grows mostly in the northern flat regions of Brazil, while the Juçara grows in the mountainous south-east regions of Brazil anywhere from Espirito Santo down to Rio Grande do Sul.
metas.footer: Click -> Euterpe Edulis for more information!

metas.name: Licuala Ramsayi
metas.note: The Queensland fan palm or Australian fan palm, is a species endemic to northeastern Queensland, Australia (Specially around Cairns).
metas.footer: Click -> Queensland Fan Palm for more information!

metas.name: Macaw Palm
metas.note: The species is found from southern Mexico and the Caribbean to Brazil, extending down to Paraguay and northern Argentina. It is commonly mistaken to be a "Paraguay Palm" (Acrocomia Totai). The key difference is that the trunk of the "Paraguay Palm" is often smoother and less irregular. The crown can also give some hints although it's difficult to catch the differences - Macaw Palm: More open and irregular, with leaves spreading in different directions. - "Paraguay Palm": Denser and more compact, sometimes looking neater and rounder.
metas.footer: Click -> Acrocomia Aculeata for more information!

metas.name: Makalani Palm
metas.note: This palm is similar to the Ilala Palm (H. Coriacea) the main difference is the shape of the stem, which regularly bulges out below the foliage. Its habitat, as seen in Geoguessr, is mostly in the northern half of Botswana and northern Limpopo.
metas.footer: Click -> Hyphaene Petersiana for more information!

metas.name: Mediterranean Fan Palm
metas.note: Chamaerops humilis is one of only two palm species native to continental Europe, the other being Phoenix theophrasti. It is mainly found in southwestern Europe, in mediterranean coasts.
metas.footer: Click -> Chamaerops Humilis for more information!

metas.name: Mexican Palmetto
metas.note: This palm seems to be prominent in coastal Texas, the east and the south coast of Mexico, Yucatán peninsula, and Guatemala. The key difference between this one and the other Sabal palms is the shape and arrangement of the leaves. Sabal Mexicana has large, stiff, pointy leaves and densely packed. Sabal Yapa has droopy, hanging leaves that almost look shredded at the tips. Sabal Rosei tends to have visible gaps between the leaves, and they are a brighter green color.
metas.footer: Click -> Sabal Mexicana for more information!

metas.name: Moriche Palm
metas.note: Mauritia flexuosa is found in the wild in streetview in: Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador and Peru.
metas.footer: Click -> Mauritia Flexuosa for more information!

metas.name: Nibong Palm
metas.note: The Nibong palm is found in Southeast Asia: Southern Thailand and Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia, and Philippines, always west of the Wallace Line. There seems to be a high concentration of them in Sumatra, Kalimantan, Peninsular Malaysia, and Java (according to Palmpedia.net).
metas.footer: Click -> Oncosperma Tigillarium for more information!

metas.name: Nikau Palm
metas.note: Rhopalostylis sapida, commonly known as nīkau, is a palm tree endemic to New Zealand, and the only palm native to mainland New Zealand.
metas.footer: Click -> Rhopalostylis Sapida for more information!

metas.name: Quindio Wax Palm
metas.note: The Quindío wax palm, is the tallest palm tree in the world and it is native to the humid montane forests of the Andes in Colombia and Peru.
metas.footer: Click -> Ceroxylon Quindiuense for more information!

metas.name: Sabal Rosei (Nayarit Palm)
metas.note: Sabal Rosei is native to the Pacific coast of Mexico, from Sinaloa to Jalisco but mostly concentrated in the state of Nayarit. The key difference between this one and the other Sabal palms is the shape and arrangement of the leaves. Sabal Rosei tends to have visible gaps between the leaves, and they are a brighter green color. Sabal Yapa has droopy, hanging leaves that almost look shredded at the tips. Sabal Mexicana has large, stiff, pointy leaves and densely packed.
metas.footer: Click -> Sabal Rosei for more information!

metas.name: Sand Palm
metas.note: The sand palm is endemic to the north of the Northern Territory of Australia, from the Fitzmaurice River to Cape Arnhem and inland as far as Katherine.
metas.footer: Click -> Livistona Humilis for more information!

metas.name: Saw Palmetto
metas.note: It is endemic to the subtropical and tropical Southeastern United States as well as Mexico, most commonly along the south Atlantic and Gulf Coastal plains and sand hills. It grows in clumps or dense thickets in sandy coastal areas, and as undergrowth in pine woods or hardwood hammocks.
metas.footer: Click -> Serenoa Repens for more information!

metas.name: Thatch Palmetto
metas.note: This palm grows pretty much exclusively in the Yucatán peninsula. The key difference between this one and the other Sabal palms is the shape and arrangement of the leaves. Sabal Yapa has droopy, hanging leaves that almost look shredded at the tips. Sabal Mexicana has large, stiff, pointy leaves and densely packed. Sabal Rosei tends to have visible gaps between the leaves, and they are a brighter green color.
metas.footer: Click -> Sabal Yapa for more information!

metas.name: Trithrinax Campestris
metas.note: This palm shares the same habitat and common name (Caranday palm) as the Copernicia Alba. It is one of the most cold-hardy palms in the world, because it also grows in the mountains of Sierras de Córdoba and Sierras de San Luis.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Yatay Palm
metas.note: Butia yatay is a Butia palm native to southern Brazil, Uruguay and northern Argentina.
metas.footer: Click -> Butia Yatay for more information!
